title: Ankhorage Studio
summary: Provides the authoring package, project workspace, host, and application capabilities for Ankhorage apps.
purpose: Give application authors a cohesive workspace for creating, editing, validating, and operating Ankhorage projects through published package and CLI boundaries.
responsibilities: Provide Studio authoring, project, runtime, host, and administration entrypoints.
Expose capabilities for starting Studio and listing, creating, or deleting workspace projects.
Compose published Ankhorage packages into the Studio authoring experience.
boundaries: Does not replace the published contracts, runtime, surface, or deployment package boundaries it consumes.
Does not require consumers to import sibling repository source files.
Does not make repository metadata enforcement decisions.
audience: Authors building and operating Ankhorage applications.
Hosts that embed or invoke Studio capabilities.
useCases: Create and manage Studio workspace projects.
Run the local Studio host and first-party Studio application.
Author application, runtime, navigation, and administration behavior through published entrypoints.

architecture.role: A Studio-specific authoring application package that composes explicit published package boundaries.
invariants: Cross-package consumption uses declared dependencies and published APIs.
Studio capabilities are exposed through explicit package and CLI entrypoints.

limitations: Platform-native behavior depends on the configured Expo and React Native peer environment.
Repository metadata enforcement remains disabled until the organization inventory is verified.
